entries.plain: The part before the curly braces that says which elements a rule applies to, such as p or .card.
The name of a visual feature you want to change, such as color or font-size. The value comes after the colon.
Paints behind an element. background-color is the simple solid-colour version.
Controls how an element is laid out, for example block, inline, flex or none to hide it.
A layout mode that lines children up in a row or column and lets them share space.
Space outside an element, pushing other elements away from it.
Space inside an element, between its edge and its content.
A line around an element. You can set its width, style and colour together.
Rounds the corners of an element.
How large the text is. Values can use px, rem, em, or clamp() to adapt to the screen.
The typeface used for text. List a few names so the browser can fall back.
In CSS a class selector begins with a dot and styles every element that uses that class.
In CSS an id selector begins with # and targets the one element with that id.
A state that applies while the pointer is over an element.
The space between children in a flex or grid layout.
